title: Fever on chemotherapy
stem:
You are an F2 doctor on an oncology ward. You are writing up chemotherapy prescriptions for tomorrow's day-unit patients, which the pharmacy needs by 17:00.

A nurse tells you that Mr Shaw, 58, who had chemotherapy eight days ago, has just been admitted with a temperature of 38.6°C and shivering.
instruction: Choose the 3 most appropriate actions to take in this situation.

options.detailed: The prescriptions are important but not urgent compared with possible sepsis.

options.brief: Possible neutropenic sepsis is an emergency.
options.detailed: Fever after chemotherapy may be neutropenic sepsis, which can be fatal without prompt treatment.

options.text: Ask the nurse to take bloods, and give antibiotics once the neutrophil count is back.
options.detailed: Blood tests are needed, but antibiotics shouldn't wait for the results.

options.text: Make sure he gets antibiotics within an hour.
options.detailed: Guidance recommends antibiotics within one hour for suspected neutropenic sepsis, without waiting for blood results.

options.text: Ask the nurse to give paracetamol and recheck his temperature in an hour.
options.brief: May mask fever and delay treatment.
options.detailed: This delays assessment of a potential emergency.

options.text: Hand the prescriptions to another doctor who doesn't know the patients.
options.detailed: Chemotherapy prescribing needs care and information.

options.text: Ask the day unit to postpone tomorrow's patients.
options.brief: Unnecessary; the prescriptions can still be done today.
options.detailed: There's no need to postpone treatment; the prescriptions can be done after the emergency.

options.text: Let the pharmacy know the prescriptions may be a little late.
options.detailed: The chemotherapy prescriptions matter, but they can wait. Letting the pharmacy know prevents a problem tomorrow.

explanation.issue: This tests whether you prioritise a possible emergency over important routine work.
explanation.keyDetails: Fever eight days after chemotherapy suggests possible neutropenic sepsis. The prescriptions are due at 17:00.
explanation.reasoning: [B] sees him, [D] gets prompt antibiotics, and [H] informs the pharmacy. The distractors delay treatment ([A], [C], [E]), or act unsafely or unnecessarily ([F], [G]).
explanation.competing: [C] is the tempting option, but antibiotics shouldn't wait for blood results.

references.title: Suspected sepsis: recognition, diagnosis and early management (NG51)
references.publisher: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
references.note: Prompt recognition and treatment of sepsis.
